CWE-321: remember-me LoggedIn cookies encode username, password, login type, and domainId (OmAuthenticationStrategy.save/decode) and are encrypted with a repository-shipped default. Source-to-sink: openmeetings.properties remember.me.encryption.key=27574200-a56f-410a-b2c9-3aa3b4b9389a is @Value-injected in Application and passed to OmAuthenticationStrategy, which builds SunJceCrypt and crypt.setKey(encryptionKey). Cookie plaintext is therefore recoverable with the public default when an admin does not change it. Apache oss-security 2026-04-09 and OPENMEETINGS-2813 match this mechanism. Follow-up 409f74a85cadd20351d0c8e333d116446db27a12 later also ships remember.me.encryption.salt=abrakadabra, making salt deterministic; that is an aggravating change, not a different bug class.

findings: Real published CWE-321: default remember-me encryption key (and later salt) shipped in openmeetings.properties, consumed by OmAuthenticationStrategy for LoggedIn cookies that store username/password/type/domainId, with no auto-rotation until 9.0.0.

BIC is ff7f413bba288e571cf7088df3cf9e212f01c56f: first public add of remember.me.encryption.key=27574200-a56f-410a-b2c9-3aa3b4b9389a and first wiring of that key into OmAuthenticationStrategy; parent 86351d4e34504f14d88af191bd924a33c0ea073a lacks the mechanism.
409f74a85cadd20351d0c8e333d116446db27a12 (next day) adds remember.me.encryption.salt=abrakadabra; it aggravates decryptability of stolen cookies but is not the first writer of the hard-coded key.

Direct fix c407437744ec5ae3c4ae675ac0ce48dbf24f1fed removes the shipped key/salt, stores a generated key, and rotates it; ancestry places the BIC by 6.1.0 (absent from 6.0.0) and the fix in 9.0.0 (absent from 8.1.0), matching the CNA range.
